title: Academic Blocks at VIT Vellore
content: The academic buildings on the Vellore campus are: Dr. M.G.R. Block (main building, MB), Silver Jubilee Tower (SJT), Technology Tower (TT), Sri M. Visvesvaraya Building (SMV), CBMR, G.D. Naidu Block (GDN), CDMM Building, Centre for Technical Support (CTS), the Library, A.L. Mudaliar Block, Structural Engineering Laboratory, Gandhi Block and PRP Block. Every building has its own furnished labs. Room-level classroom locations are not listed on this page.

title: Campus Size and Layout
content: The VIT Vellore campus is spread over 372 acres. Academic blocks, auditoriums, canteens, sports grounds (about 20 acres) and hostels are planned across this area, and two railway underpasses connect the academic side with the hostel side.

title: Anna Auditorium
content: Anna Auditorium seats 1800 and covers about 15,436 sq ft. It is air-conditioned, has Wi-Fi, a large stage, green rooms and stage lighting, and hosts major events and conferences. It is located beside the volleyball and basketball courts and is a well-known landmark on campus.

title: Smart Classrooms
content: Smart classrooms are spacious rooms equipped with a whiteboard and a projector so faculty can switch teaching modes. They are also used for seminars and events. Specific room numbers and timetables are not published on this page; your own class venues appear in your timetable on VTOP.

title: Canteen Locations
content: There are three multi-cuisine canteens run by external caterers: one in G.D. Naidu Block, one in Silver Jubilee Tower, and one at the centre of the campus near Technology Tower. They serve home-style food at student-friendly prices.

title: Hostel Dining, Food Court and Night Canteen
content: Hostel dining areas open as early as 7:00 AM, and night canteens run from 10:30 PM to 12:30 AM. Mess food covers vegetarian, non-vegetarian and international options. A 600 sq m Food Court serves veg and non-veg food, and fast food outlets are attached to both the Men's and Women's Hostels.

title: Hostel Menu and Special Dishes
content: A balanced monthly menu is prepared by the Student Mess and Menu Committee together with hostel administrators. Students can order from a limited list of special dishes at the restaurant-style mess with prior registration. Hostel review committee meetings are held once every 15 days to take student queries and suggestions.

title: Hostel Rooms and Facilities
content: Hostels offer AC and non-AC single and shared rooms. Each room has a cot, chair, study table, study lamp, bookshelf and cupboard. On-premises amenities include an air-conditioned gym, indoor and outdoor sports, study dormitories, first aid centre, swimming pool, mechanized laundry, pharmacy, Wi-Fi, general stores, tailoring unit, photocopy facilities, beauty salon and visitor halls.

title: Hostel Safety and Late-Night Travel
content: Hostels have round-the-clock security personnel, 24-hour water and power supply backed by standby generators, and block supervisors, counsellors and maintenance staff. Security guards can accompany students between campus and the nearest railway station or bus stops during late-night or early-morning hours.

title: Health Centre Location and Services
content: The primary health centre (run by Sri Narayani Hospital and Research Centre) is in Dr. A.L. Mudaliar Block and provides round-the-clock primary care to students, staff and their dependents. The ground floor has reception, pharmacy, two OPD rooms (one male, one female), an emergency room with 3 beds and a dressing/suturing room. The first floor has specialist consultation rooms, wards with 20 in-patient beds, physiotherapy, lab and X-ray. Helpline: +91 416 220 2000 / 2217.

title: Ambulance and Emergency Numbers
content: Ambulance service runs 24 hours. Call intercom 2000, 2238 or 2217. There are 3 ambulances: one at the health centre and one each in the men's and ladies hostels. The health centre helpline is +91 416 220 2000 / 2217.

title: Central Library Overview
content: The Periyar EVR Central Library covers 7,770 sq m over six floors above the ground floor. It is fully automated with the KOHA library system, RFID self check-out and return kiosks, and a Web-OPAC catalogue at webopac.vit.ac.in. Holdings (as on 8 Oct 2026) include 2,55,853 books, 32,396 back volumes, 412 print journals and 3,75,431 e-books, plus online databases accessible on and off campus via egateway.vit.ac.in. All students, faculty and staff are members.

title: Library Rules and Borrowing
content: Wearing the ID card and biometric entry/exit are compulsory. Keep silence, do not use phones inside, and leave bags and big handbags at the entrance. Books are issued only on your own ID card, cannot be sub-lent, and one online renewal is available through Web-OPAC. Reference books, newspapers and journals stay in the library, though overnight issue is possible for selected reference books. For a lost or badly damaged book you must replace it or pay double the recent price plus handling charges.

title: Library Timings
content: The Periyar EVR Central Library is open from 7:30 AM to 12:30 AM every day of the year. Book issue and return counters work 7:30 AM to 8:00 PM on weekdays and 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays. E-resources can be accessed any time through egateway.vit.ac.in.

title: Library Floor Plan
content: Ground floor: Circulation Help Desk, self check-out/check-in kiosks, periodicals, Braille section and Web-OPAC. First floor: Reference section and reading hall. Second floor: Stack Area I (Engineering and Technology), reading hall, Alumni Book Bank. Third floor: Stack Area II (Science and Humanities), videoconferencing hall, scholars' wing, Media Resource Centre. Fourth and fifth floors: reading halls. Sixth floor: back volumes and rare books.

title: Library E-Resources and Remote Access
content: Subscribed e-resources include IEEE, ScienceDirect, Springer Nature, Scopus, Web of Science, ACM, ASCE, ASME, Wiley and many more, with on- and off-campus access through egateway.vit.ac.in. The MyLOFT mobile app gives access to online databases, and Mendeley reference management is available. The page also links NPTEL, NDL India, SWAYAM Prabha and other open e-learning resources.

title: Sports Facilities on Campus
content: Outdoor: 400 m athletics track, 3 soccer fields, 2 cricket grounds, 2 hockey fields, floodlit badminton (18 men's, 6 women's), basketball (1 synthetic plus 5), 8 handball, 4 tennis, volleyball and throwball courts. Indoor: wooden-floor badminton, table tennis boards, 3 air-conditioned snooker tables, squash courts and several air-conditioned fitness centres and gyms. Aquatics: a 50 m x 25 m men's pool and a 25 m x 12.5 m women's pool, both floodlit.

title: Physical Education Department and Gym
content: The Department of Physical Education (set up in 1984) is in the VIT Shopping Complex, which has an air-conditioned gymnasium and a snooker hall. Separate fitness centres exist in the men's and women's hostels. Contact: Director, Physical Education, director.sports@vit.ac.in, phone 0416 220 117 / 0416 220 2242. The department runs intramural tournaments, selection trials for university teams and sports scholarships.

title: Campus Transport
content: University buses carry students to locations in and around Vellore, which helps day scholars reach college on time, and shuttle cabs run around the campus during active hours of the day. Bus routes, stop timings, pass procedure and fees are not given on the official amenities page, so those need to be confirmed with the transport office.

title: Event Registration on VIT Events Portal
content: Register at events.vit.ac.in. New users sign up with a valid email address, activate the account using the email sent to them, then fill in their details. A registration is accepted only after the event fee is paid, and payment and file uploads close on or before the date given for each event. You can delete a registration before paying but not after. Invoices can be downloaded only after payment, and your transactions are under Your name > Profile > Transactions.

title: Bonafide, Migration, Transcript and Other Certificates
content: The Controller of Examinations (COE) office handles Bonafide Certificates, Migration Certificates (ara@vit.ac.in), Instruction Medium Certificates, backlog certificates, duplicate certificates and original documents including the Transfer Certificate. Transcripts are requested via vit.ac.in/transcripts-alumni, and certificate verification is at web.vit.ac.in/CertificateVerification/login. VIT does not issue rank certificates except to the top three rank holders. The exact bonafide application steps are not described on the page; see the COE Email Contacts page for the current contact.

title: IT Policy and Centre for Technical Support
content: The Centre for Technical Support (CTS) maintains the policies for using VIT's computing and network resources, covering the library, computer labs, offices, hostels and guest houses wherever the network is provided. All students, staff and authorised visitors must follow the guidelines, and violations can lead to disciplinary action. The CTS office is in Room 103 on the 1st floor of the CTS Block.

content: Visitors and parents can use the VIT Guest House (guesthouse.vit.ac.in). The website also has a Hotels in Vellore page (vit.ac.in/hotels-in-vellore) for other stay options. Rates and booking steps are on those pages, not in this knowledge base.

title: Beware of Fake VIT Websites
content: VIT warns against fraudulent calls, emails, SMS, WhatsApp and social media messages, and against fake websites misusing the VITEEE name or claiming direct admission. The only official website is vit.ac.in.

title: Library Borrowing Limits and Late Fines
content: Books you can hold at one time: UG students 4, PG students 5, research scholars 5, faculty 6, staff 2. One online renewal is allowed. The policy lists late-return fines for students and scholars of Rs. 1 per day per book for days 1 to 7 and Rs. 2 per day per book for days 8 to 14, and double the book's cost if it is not returned by day 57. The self-issue system locks when a student's fine reaches Rs. 100. The same policy also says no fine system applies but no-dues is withheld until books are returned, so please confirm the current fine with the library.

title: Lost ID Card: Where to Look First
content: If you lose your ID card, first ask at the security office of the particular academic block where you may have lost it, such as the one at the SJT entrance for SJT, and also check the SCORE office. If you lost it anywhere other than the academic buildings, check with the main security office. If it is not found at these places, go to the CTS office to get a replacement.
